title: fix: stop pending Signal sends after caller cancellation
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Pending Signal deliveries can continue after their originating caller is canceled or superseded. The shared delivery owner checks the caller before entering the adapter, but Signal can then await reply lookup, media preparation, socket setup, or a rejected native quote before starting its next request. Dropping the caller's check across those steps lets an obsolete delivery reach the daemon.

Fixes #151114.

## User Impact

Signal text, attachments, formatted message chunks, and reaction additions or removals honor the originating delivery's existing lifetime check at the request boundary. A caller that ends during preparation cannot start the next request, including an unquoted fallback after a definitive quote rejection.

A request already submitted is allowed to settle, and its accepted result is preserved. Earlier delivered chunks remain reported even when later chunks are blocked. Account selection, recipient policy, available actions, and Signal's native payload formats keep their existing behavior; this change adds no configuration or scheduled-action capability.

## Why This Change Was Made

Core already supplies `assertDirectAdapterHandoff` for task-progress sends, agent final delivery, and durable delivery custody. Signal now carries that same callback through its registered message and outbound adapters, quote fallback, and reaction helpers to the native HTTP, Unix RPC, and container REST request writers.

The transport performs the check after its own preparation. This matters for Unix socket opening and for the container's additional attachment read and base64 conversion, which happen below the shared send helper. The formatted send functions use the existing SDK parameter types, and container mutation helpers share their existing request-option type. This keeps the caller and timeout fields together instead of maintaining separate copies.

## Evidence

Against unchanged production, fourteen cancellation regressions fail because a later request is submitted after the caller closes; 51 controls pass. The corrected behavior has 152 distinct focused passing cases, including registered message and legacy outbound adapters, cancellation during approved media reads and container attachment conversion, native quote fallback, reaction addition/removal, and accepted results or earlier delivered chunks. These tests use real HTTP and Unix sockets with synthetic daemon responses and task-owned media.

The [full Signal CI lane](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35278027014/job/105393539767) passed 972 tests across 52 files. Its three skips are existing macOS ACL tests on Linux; the cancellation regressions and requested send, reaction, client, transport-adapter and media-limit tests all ran. The [production type graph](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35278027014/job/105393540211), [test type graph](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35278027014/job/105393540193), Signal's typed-lint shard, docs and [runtime/plugin build](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35278027014/job/105393539531) passed.

The 13-command publication preflight passed remotely in 54.1 seconds. Eight remaining selected checks also passed on the exact candidate tree: changelog attribution, extension re-export boundaries, dependency pins, the two Doctor contract test files (six cases), plugin boundaries, media download helpers and runtime sidecar loaders. Together with the successful CI jobs, this completes the selected final validation plan.

CI tested merge 090e94e5f1394743f72dfe332649c564425e04bc containing head b81596a342b8659bf8e51b1d6a46869974ec559b. The Signal source, shared callback/result owners, harness configuration and locked dependencies match the candidate; the later target changes were checked for compatibility with those paths. Independent source review found no actionable P0–P2 defects, and the [completed ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/151169#issuecomment-5721686024) rated this head Platinum with no findings.
